## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization of the per-particle update can survive the branchy-respawn loop and approach the streaming bandwidth ceiling.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 7.625 (N=10000, within L2) to 5.933 (N=100000, just past the L2 spill at N≈60787) as fixed overhead amortizes, then stays flat at ~5.95 through N=10M — no knee at the L2→DRAM transition. The L1d spill at N≈949 is below the smallest measured N, so its effect is invisible. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: at q=0.5 the best ns/p holds ~10.3–11.1 across all N, still flat past the L2 spill. The N-shape is dominated by overhead amortization, not cache hierarchy.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 11.63 GB/s (N=100000, q=0.01) = 39% of the 29.9 GB/s streaming ceiling. At q=0.01 the algo sustains 11.4–11.6 GB/s from N=100000 to N=10M, never approaching the ceiling. Increasing death rate monotonically degrades bandwidth: peak falls to 10.2 GB/s (q=0.1), 8.4 GB/s (q=0.25), 6.7 GB/s (q=0.5). The algo is compute-bound at low q (66.7% compute at N=10M, q=0.01) and transitions to branch-bound at high q (branch_flush 20.5–22.8% at q=0.5). It is never bandwidth-bound.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the per-particle physics. The update loop (0x10004dab8+) operates on scalar `s` registers: `ldp s5, s6`, `fadd s5`, `fmul s5`, `fcvtzs`, with per-component `fcmp`/`csel` clamping. The scatter is byte-granular read-modify-write: `ldrb w2, [x1]`, `add w2, w2, w12`, `cmp w2, #0xff`, `csel`, `strb w2, [x1]` — three bytes per neighbor, no vectorization. The only vectorized code is the death-flag batch scan (0x10004dd1c+): `ldp q1, q0` loads 32 flags, `orr.16b`/`ext.16b`/`orr.8b` reduce them to a single test. No gather (`ld1` indexed) appears. The scalar FMA and byte-granular scatter explain why bandwidth stalls at 39% of ceiling: each neighbor update is a scalar load-add-clamp-store cycle that cannot stream.

## Verdict
Refuted — the compiler did not auto-vectorize the per-particle update. The physics loop uses scalar `s`-register `fmul`/`fadd` and byte-granular `ldrb`/`strb` scatter, capping bandwidth at 11.63 GB/s = 39% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling even at q=0.01 with no cache-spill knee. Only the death-flag scan was vectorized (`ldp q`, `orr.16b`). At q=0.5, branch_flush rises to 20.5% and bandwidth falls to 6.7 GB/s, confirming the branchy respawn prevents auto-vectorization from approaching the streaming ceiling in any regime.
